docs.title: scMultiBench
docs.text:
scMultiBench is a benchmark of single-cell multimodal integration methods. The multibench package runs them from Python and scores their output with the benchmark's metrics. 

pip install multibench-sc

Get started How it works

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: The package is imported as import multibench as mtb. Its functions form four groups, methods, run, metrics and figures, plus a setup group. Each name links to its reference entry, with the parameters and examples.

docs.title: 1. Methods
docs.text:
call returns mtb.find_methods(category, modalities=, needs_labels=) The method ids that fit. mtb.method_info(method) Its language, env, GPU use, labels, ATAC form, variants and runtime. mtb.params_for(method, category, modalities) What params= can set, with each default. 
import multibench as mtb

mtb.find_methods("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"], needs_labels=False)
mtb.params_for("Matilda", "vertical", ["rna", "adt"])["tunable"]

docs.title: 2. Run (Linux or Windows)
docs.text:
call returns mtb.scan(dataset, category, methods=, params=) The plan, one row per method: can it run here and why not. command=True adds its command. mtb.run(dataset, category, out_dir, methods=, params=) A RunResult, also saved in out_dir. mtb.load_run(out_dir) The RunResult saved in out_dir. mtb.RunResult summary, long, embedding(method), plot(), rescore(), save() and records, one dict per method with its status, parameters, label order and provenance. 
mtb.data.fetch("D11")
mtb.scan("D11", "vertical")
res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", out_dir="out/",
              methods=["Matilda", "totalVI"], params={"Matilda": {"epochs": 10}})
res.summary
emb = res.embedding("Matilda")      # obsm["X_emb"]; obs: each cell's label (and batch)

A dataset is a folder: its path, or its name under mtb.config.data_path. One method is methods=["Matilda"].

docs.title: 3. Metrics
docs.text:
call returns mtb.evaluate(embedding, labels, method=, dataset=, category=) The scores, as the long table. mtb.load_results(category, dataset=) The stored results, as the long table. mtb.rank(category, long_df=) The overall score and row order of mtb.plot.bubble, best first. mtb.catalog.metrics() The metric codes and their families. 
import pandas as pd

# your run of Matilda on D11, next to the stored results of D11
mine = mtb.evaluate("out/Matilda_D11/embedding.h5", dataset="D11",
                    category="vertical", method="Matilda (this run)")
both = pd.concat([mtb.load_results("vertical"), mine])
mtb.rank("vertical", long_df=both)

docs.title: 4. Figures
docs.text:
call returns mtb.plot.bubble(long_df, metrics=, methods=) The paper's bubble table. mtb.plot.bar(long_df, metrics=, methods=) One bar per method. 
mtb.plot.bubble(both, metrics="clustering", save="vertical.pdf")

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: call does mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, folder, ...) Writes an AnnData or MuData as a dataset folder. mtb.io.read(path) Reads a dataset file or an embedding.h5 as an AnnData. mtb.data.fetch(*datasets) Downloads demo datasets and returns each dataset's folder. mtb.data.write_example(dataset) Writes a tutorial's example .h5ad files. mtb.catalog.datasets() The datasets to fetch or with stored results, with their category. mtb.env.install(methods, dry_run=) Installs the methods' envs. dry_run=True shows each env's state and size. mtb.config The settings: data_path, repo_path, envs_dir and leiden_flavor. print(mtb.config) shows them.

docs.title: The long table and metrics=
docs.text:
evaluate, load_results and RunResult.long return the same columns: metric, value, method, dataset, category and source ("stored" or "user") and scored_with. The figures and rank read any such table. Next to stored results, name your rows apart, such as mine.assign(method=mine.method + " (this run)"), and score them with dataset= of the stored dataset.

metrics= takes a family, a code, or a list of codes and families:

family codes "clustering" ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI "batch" ASW_batch, ARI_batch, NMI_batch, GC, iLISI, kBET "classification" OCA, ACA, Spec, Sens, F1

"all" is the three families, and kBET runs only when named. Higher is better for every metric.

docs.title: Source code
docs.text:
• Benchmark and method scripts: https://github.com/PYangLab/scMultiBench
  • The multibench API, this documentation, the tutorials and the PyPI releases: https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench, a fork of the repository above

To cite the software, set version and year to the release you used (multibench.__version__).

software.bib
@software{scmultibench_code,
  author    = {Liu, Chunlei and Ding, Sichang and Yang, Pengyi},
  title     = {{scMultiBench}: a benchmark and Python API for single-cell
               multimodal omics integration},
  url       = {https://github.com/PYangLab/scMultiBench},
  note      = {multibench Python package,
               https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench},
  version   = {<multibench.__version__>},
  year      = {2026}
}
Details: reporting a run

Record the package version (multibench.__version__), each method's environment, and the command it ran (the command column of mtb.scan(..., command=True)).

run saves one record per method under out_dir. The record holds the environment and its build (cpu, gpu or single), the parameters, the package version, the version of the method scripts and the computer. The scored_with column of the table mtb.evaluate returns names its Leiden backend, clustering and package version.

The stored results carry the package version that scored them in df.attrs["rerun_version"].

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Error messages and their fixes are under Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Do I install the environments again next time?
docs.text: No. mtb.env.install keeps each environment on disk, and later sessions use it: mtb.run finds it, and mtb.env.install skips it. Only Google Colab starts empty, because Colab deletes the disk with the runtime.

docs.title: Where are the environments?
docs.text:
In mtb.config.envs_dir, one folder per environment:

import multibench as mtb
print(mtb.config.envs_dir)
mtb.env.install(["scJoint"], dry_run=True)   # its environment, and "have" once installed

Method environments says which folder envs_dir is.

docs.title: Can I use an environment outside multibench?
docs.text:
Yes. Each one is an ordinary conda environment. Activate it by its path, for example to run a method's own code or your own script with the same packages:

conda activate /path/to/envs_dir/scmb_scjoint
python my_script.py
conda deactivate

When envs_dir is your conda's envs folder, the name works too: conda activate scmb_scjoint.

Install extra packages in an environment of your own, not in these: a changed environment can change the methods' results.

docs.title: Can several people share one set of environments?
docs.text:
Yes. Install them once into a shared folder, and give everyone the same setting before they import multibench:

export MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR=/shared/multibench_envs

The person who installs needs write access to the folder.

docs.title: How do I remove an environment?
docs.text: Delete its folder in envs_dir. The .layers folder there holds files that several PyTorch environments share; delete it only with the last of them.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install multibench-sc installs the API on Python 3.9 or newer. Methods run on Linux, such as Google Colab, and on Windows for the methods listed there. On macOS you can use the stored results, check your data with scan, score embeddings and plot.

docs.title: Quick setup
docs.text:
One block creates an environment, installs multibench with JupyterLab and adds a Jupyter kernel named multibench. Steps 1 to 3 below explain its lines.

Linux and macOS, condaLinux and macOS, venvWindows, PowerShell terminal
conda create -n multibench python=3.12 -y
conda activate multibench
pip install multibench-sc jupyterlab
python -m ipykernel install --user --name multibench
python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)"
terminal
python3 -m venv ~/multibench-env
source ~/multibench-env/bin/activate
pip install multibench-sc jupyterlab
python -m ipykernel install --user --name multibench
python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)"
PowerShell
py -m venv "$HOME\multibench-env"
$py = "$HOME\multibench-env\Scripts\python.exe"
& $py -m pip install multibench-sc jupyterlab
& $py -m ipykernel install --user --name multibench
& $py -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)"

The last line prints the installed version. jupyter lab then opens JupyterLab (on Windows, & "$HOME\multibench-env\Scripts\jupyter-lab.exe"). In a notebook, choose the kernel multibench. To run a method, install its environment next: see Method environments.

python3 and py start a Python that is already installed. The tutorials are run with Python 3.12. On Windows, py is the launcher that the python.org installer adds, and py -3.12 asks for that version. If PowerShell does not know py, write python in the first line.

docs.title: With an AI assistant
docs.text:
An AI coding assistant that runs commands on your computer can do the setup for you. Give it this prompt:

prompt
Set up the Python package multibench on this computer and show me that it works.

Facts
- PyPI name: multibench-sc. Import: import multibench as mtb. It needs
  Python 3.9 or newer.
- Docs: https://dsichang.github.io/scMultiBench/installation/
- multibench runs single-cell integration methods. Methods run on Linux and,
  for the methods the docs list, on Windows. On macOS no method runs; stored
  results, data checks, scoring and plots work.
- Each method runs in its own environment. mtb.env.install(["<method>"])
  downloads it as a prebuilt archive: no conda, compiler or administrator
  rights needed. print(mtb.config) shows where it goes (envs_dir: conda's
  envs folder when conda is on PATH, else ~/.cache/multibench/envs).

Rules
- Make one new environment named multibench. With conda installed:
  conda create -n multibench python=3.12. Without conda: a venv in
  ~/multibench-env from a Python that is already installed, 3.12 or newer
  if there is one, else 3.9 or newer. If there is none, stop and ask me to
  install Python.
- Install nothing else on the computer: no Python, no package manager,
  nothing into the base or system Python. No sudo, no administrator rights.
  If a conda environment named multibench, the folder ~/multibench-env or a
  Jupyter kernel named multibench already exists, stop and ask me.
- In every command, call the environment's python by its full path instead
  of relying on activation. On Windows that is Scripts\python.exe in a venv
  and python.exe in a conda environment's own folder.
- Ask me before you install a method environment, and tell me its size:
  mtb.env.install([...], dry_run=True) shows it. Ask me before you fetch a
  dataset larger than 100 MB.
- Steps 2 and 5 take several minutes each. Wait for them, and do not start
  them again.
- When a command fails, show me the error and what you would try next. Do
  not skip a check to get past a failure.

Steps
1. Tell me the operating system and whether conda is installed.
2. Create the environment and install into it:
   python -m pip install multibench-sc jupyterlab
3. Add the Jupyter kernel: python -m ipykernel install --user --name multibench
4. Check, on any system:
   python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__); print(mtb.config); print(len(mtb.load_results('cross', dataset='D52')), 'stored result rows')"
   It prints the version, the folders multibench uses and a row count above 0.
5. On Linux or Windows, after my yes, run one method on a 2 MB demo dataset.
   Save these lines as multibench_check.py and run the file with the
   environment's python:
     import multibench as mtb
     mtb.data.fetch("D52mini")
     mtb.env.install(["StabMap"])
     res = mtb.run("D52mini", "cross", methods=["StabMap"], out_dir="multibench_check")
     print(res.summary.T.to_string())
   The status must be "scored". On Windows, cLISI and iLISI are empty without
   a C++ compiler: that is expected. On macOS, skip this step and say why.

Then report: the environment's location, the multibench version, the kernel
name, the outcome of step 5, and the commands that remove the environment,
the kernel, the folders that print(mtb.config) names and the files of step 5.

docs.title: Step 1: Create an isolated environment
docs.text:
Any fresh Python 3.9+ environment works. Conda is optional: the method environments install without it.

Condavenv terminal
conda create -n multibench python=3.12 -y
conda activate multibench
terminal
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

On Windows, activate it with .venv\Scripts\activate.

docs.title: Step 2: Install multibench
docs.text:
terminal
pip install multibench-sc
Dependencies

The install brings numpy, pandas, h5py, anndata, matplotlib, pyyaml, scanpy and scib. PyTorch, R and the method packages are not installed here. Each method's environment holds them.

Developer install

Clone the repository only to edit the notebooks or run the test suite:

terminal
git clone https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench.git
cd scMultiBench
pip install -e ".[dev]" --config-settings editable_mode=compat

docs.title: Step 3: Verify the install
docs.text:
terminal
python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)"

These calls need no method environment:

import multibench as mtb

print(mtb.find_methods(category="vertical"))

Dataset folder layout shows how to lay out your own dataset.

docs.title: Method environments
docs.text:
Each method runs in its own environment. Install only the ones you need. mtb.env.install downloads prebuilt archives, with no conda needed.

import multibench as mtb

# the environments a category needs: installed or not, with their sizes
mtb.env.install(category="vertical", dry_run=True)
# one method
mtb.env.install(["StabMap"])
# one category
mtb.env.install(category="vertical")
Details
  • mtb.config.envs_dir is where they go: $MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR when set, else the writable envs directory of the conda or mamba on PATH, else ~/.cache/multibench/envs. print(mtb.config) shows the folder in use.
  • A failed archive download falls back to a build from the lockfile, which needs conda or mamba and takes longer.
  • flavor="cpu" or "gpu" picks the build. flavor="gpu" installs the GPU build from a host without a GPU, such as a cluster login node; by default such a host gets the CPU build.
  • The totals of the dry run: categories share environments, so two categories cost less than the sum of their totals.
  • mtb.env.install skips environments that already exist, so a rerun resumes an interrupted install. With no methods and no category, it installs all 24. Check the total with the dry run first (reference).
Details: method scripts

mtb.env.install downloads the method scripts with the environments, and a run downloads them if they are missing. They go to mtb.config.repo_path, which is ~/.cache/multibench/scMultiBench_scripts/<id> after pip install. The variable MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF instead fetches a given commit or tag of PYangLab/scMultiBench with git.

On a host without network, run mtb.env.install on a connected machine that sees the same home folder, or copy mtb.config.repo_path from one and set MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH to the copy.

docs.title: Google Colab
docs.text:
The tutorials open in Colab from their badge and run on its default CPU runtime. Each notebook installs the environments of the methods it runs and runs them, with no conda needed.

Details

On a GPU runtime, an environment that has a GPU build gets that build: a larger download, and faster training.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
mtb.env.install and mtb.run also work on Windows, without conda, WSL or administrator rights, for these methods (tested on Windows 11):

Windows environment Methods A CPU build and a GPU build Matilda, sciPENN, Cobolt, Multigrate, MultiVI, totalVI, scMDC, scMoMaT, MultiMAP, uniPort, Portal A GPU build only: the method needs an NVIDIA GPU, as on Linux moETM, SMILE, iPOLNG, scBridge, sciCAN, UnitedNet One build, on the CPU StabMap, iNMF, online_iNMF, Conos, Seurat_v5, Seurat_WNN, MOFA2, scMSI, scMVP, VIMCCA, VIPCCA

UINMF, SCALEX, Concerto, scMM, GLUE, scJoint, Seurat_v3 and MIRA run on Linux only. Asked for on Windows, they are refused: "<method> has no Windows environment. Run it on a Linux machine, such as Colab."

Details
  • Name the methods to install. mtb.env.install(category=...) and the call without methods are refused on Windows, because every category has a method that runs on Linux only.
  • Keep the path of mtb.config.envs_dir short. Windows limits a file path to 259 characters, and mtb.env.install refuses a folder that leaves too little room.
  • Nothing is built on Windows: build=True is refused, and a download that fails raises an error.
  • PyTorch needs the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. Install it if a method stops because a DLL is missing.
  • A user name with a space can stop the R methods (StabMap, Seurat, iNMF and Conos). Set TMPDIR to a folder without a space before you start Python.
  • cLISI and iLISI need a C++ compiler on Windows, such as the g++ of Rtools. Without one they are NaN, with a warning (Troubleshooting).

docs.title: Get the data
docs.text:
Each tutorial downloads its dataset on first run. Datasets go to mtb.config.data_path: ~/.cache/multibench/data after pip install, <repo>/data in a developer install.

import multibench as mtb

mtb.catalog.datasets().dataset.tolist()   # ['D11', 'D28', 'D45', 'D46', 'D52', 'D22mini', ...]
mtb.data.fetch("D11")                     # no-op when already present
Details

The tutorials run on one dataset per integration task. D11 is a benchmark dataset; each mini is a smaller copy of one, with a subset of its cells, genes and peaks:

Task Dataset Size vertical, RNA + ADT D11 11 MB vertical, RNA + ATAC D27mini_vertical 24 MB vertical, RNA + ADT + ATAC D22mini 8 MB diagonal, [RNA, ATAC] D27mini 15 MB diagonal, [multiple RNA, multiple ATAC] D37mini 12 MB mosaic, [RNA, RNA + ADT, ADT] D38mini 2 MB mosaic, [RNA, RNA + ATAC, ATAC] D45mini 11 MB mosaic, Mixed, with shared modality D46mini 4 MB mosaic, Mixed, without shared modality D49mini 5 MB cross, Multiple RNA + ADT D52mini 2 MB cross, Multiple RNA + ATAC D56mini 10 MB cross, Multiple ADT + ATAC D58mini 7 MB cross, Multiple RNA + ADT + ATAC D59mini 8 MB

The benchmark datasets D28 (diagonal, 137 MB), D45 (mosaic, 290 MB), D46 (mosaic, 97 MB) and D52 (cross, 179 MB) are also fetchable.

MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH sets the data path. Without it, and with XDG_CACHE_HOME set, the data path after pip install is $XDG_CACHE_HOME/multibench/data. print(mtb.config) shows the path in use.

To download a dataset by hand, for example D11:

terminal
DATA=~/.cache/multibench/data   # the data_path that print(mtb.config) shows
URL=https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench/releases/download/data-v1
mkdir -p "$DATA"
wget -qO- "$URL/D11.tar.gz" | tar xz -C "$DATA"

The full collection of processed datasets is linked from the scMultiBench README. Unpack a dataset under the data path, or anywhere else and pass its folder path as dataset.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
OSError: Environment <env> of <method> is not installed

The method's environment is missing. Run the install command the message names, for example mtb.env.install(["<method>"]). mtb.scan() names it per method.

Environment <env> was not installed by this version of multibench

A conda environment has the name of a method's environment, but this version of multibench did not install it, so it is not used: an environment you made yourself, or one that multibench 0.3.9 or older built from a recipe, or 0.3.0 or older unpacked from an archive. Rename or remove the folder the message names, then run mtb.env.install(["<method>"]).

OSError: Methods run only on Linux ...

Methods cannot run on macOS. Run the call on a Linux machine. Make the commands there: mtb.scan(..., command=True) writes this computer's paths into them. mtb.env.install raises the same error.

OSError: <method> has no Windows environment ...

The method runs on Linux only. Windows lists the methods that run on Windows.

OSError naming envs_dir, with MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE=prefix

Prefix mode is forced, but the environment is not under envs_dir. Install it (mtb.env.install(["<method>"])), point MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR at the folder that holds it, or unset MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE.

RuntimeError: Conda is not installed on this computer. build=True needs it.

Only a lockfile build needs conda. Leave out build=True.

ImportError: No module named scib from mtb.evaluate

multibench was installed with --no-deps or into another interpreter. Run pip install multibench-sc in the environment you import from.

TypingError: Failed in nopython mode pipeline ..., naming knn_dists

Scoring builds a neighbour graph with scanpy, and umap-learn 0.6.0 fails there with scanpy 1.12.5 on 8,192 cells or more. mtb.evaluate raises the error, and a run ends with the status ran and the error in reason. Install another umap-learn release:

terminal
pip install "umap-learn!=0.6.0"

Then call evaluate again, or score a finished run with mtb.load_run(out_dir).rescore().

AttributeError: 'csr_array' object has no attribute 'getnnz'

On Python 3.9 to 3.11, pynndescent 0.7.0 fails with the scanpy those Pythons get, on 8,192 cells or more. Python 3.9 reports it as ValueError: Cannot add edge .... Install the pynndescent line before it:

terminal
pip install "pynndescent<0.7"

Then call evaluate again, or score a finished run with mtb.load_run(out_dir).rescore(). An environment with Python 3.12 or newer is not affected.

cLISI / iLISI are NaN, with a warning naming knn_graph.o

Both need scib's compiled LISI helper, which ships as a Linux x86-64 binary. On other platforms evaluate() rebuilds it automatically when a C++ compiler (g++, c++ or clang++) is on PATH.

Without a compiler, install one (Xcode command-line tools on macOS, the g++ of Rtools on Windows) and rerun evaluate in a new Python session, or run the g++ command the warning prints. The other metrics are computed either way.

unsupported input format

mtb.io.export_dataset takes an in-memory AnnData or MuData. Read other formats into an AnnData first.

If the problem remains, open an issue with the output of python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)" and pip freeze.

Next: the Quickstart, or run a method with Run a method.

docs.title: How scMultiBench works
docs.text: scMultiBench is a benchmark of single-cell multimodal integration methods. The multibench package is its Python API.

docs.title: What scMultiBench covers
docs.text:
The benchmark groups datasets into four categories (category in the API) by how the data were measured: vertical, diagonal, mosaic and cross. The four integration categories defines each.

Details

Its datasets are real and simulated, and cover RNA, ADT and ATAC.

docs.title: How it evaluates
docs.text:
The benchmark scores dimension reduction, batch correction, clustering and classification. In the package, grand_score combines the scores: on each dataset, each metric ranks a method's value among the stored methods' values. The mean of a method's ranks is min-max scaled, so that the best stored method gets 1 and the lowest 0, and your own rows are placed on that scale. grand_score is the mean over the datasets a method was scored on. It is a rank, not a quality score. For the full ranking per category, see the paper's decision tree (Fig. 6) or the interactive explorer.

Details

The metric panels are:

  • Dimension reduction, batch correction and clustering: scIB metrics such as kBET, iLISI, ASW, graph connectivity, ARI and NMI.
  • Classification: OCA, ACA, Spec, Sens and F1.
  • Every method: runtime and peak memory.

In the package, mtb.evaluate computes the scIB metrics and the classification metrics for an embedding.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Five steps take you from finding methods to plotting your run next to the stored results. Only step 3 runs a method. It needs Linux or Windows and a method environment. The other steps also work on macOS.

For your own data:

  • CITE-seq: the RNA + ADT tutorial, which runs in Colab.
  • 10x Multiome, unpaired RNA + ATAC or one file per batch: see Your own data as a dataset folder.
Words used on this site embedding A table with one row per cell and tens to hundreds of numbers per cell, like adata.obsm["X_pca"]. category How your cells were measured, for example vertical for CITE-seq from one experiment. variant One version of a method for one data type, such as RNA + ADT. role The name of one input file, such as rna or adt. dataset folder One folder that holds the input files of a dataset, such as rna.h5 and cty.csv. raw counts Integer counts per cell and feature, before any normalization. demo dataset A dataset that mtb.data.fetch downloads: a benchmark dataset such as D11, or a smaller mini copy of one such as D22mini. stored results The scores that ship with the package: its own runs of the methods, one dataset per category. long table A table with one row per method, dataset and metric. cell order The order of the rows in a method's output. For diagonal data most methods put the RNA cells first, then the ATAC cells. run writes each cell's barcode into embedding.h5, and evaluate(dataset=) matches the label files by them. 
import multibench as mtb, pandas as pd

# 1. methods for RNA + ADT measured in several batches (cross)
mtb.find_methods(category="cross", modalities=["rna", "adt"])

# 2. plot the stored results of dataset D52
df = mtb.load_results("cross", dataset="D52")
mtb.plot.bubble(df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "cLISI"], save="fig.pdf")

# 3. run and score a method on D52 (Linux or Windows)
mtb.data.fetch("D52")
mtb.env.install(["StabMap"])
res = mtb.run("D52", "cross", methods=["StabMap"], out_dir="out/")

# 4. score an embedding of your own (adata: your AnnData)
scores = mtb.evaluate(adata, labels="celltype", obsm="X_pca", method="PCA")

# 5. plot your run of step 3 next to the stored results
mine = res.long.assign(method=res.long.method + " (this run)")
mtb.plot.bubble(pd.concat([df, mine]), metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "cLISI"])
  1. Discover methods covers filtering the methods by category, modality and labels, and ranking them on the stored results.
  2. Load and plot results covers loading the stored results and drawing the paper's bubble table.
  3. Run a method covers running a method on a demo dataset or on your own data.
  4. Score an embedding covers what each metric measures and what evaluate takes.
  5. Add your own method covers putting your scores next to the stored ones, and Are my numbers comparable? what to expect.

Read the stored results and rank the methods of a category. Are my numbers comparable? says what to expect when you add your own runs.

Name Summary mtb.load_results Load the stored results as one long table. mtb.rank The overall score and row order of mtb.plot.bubble, best first.

docs.title: mtb.load_results
docs.text:
load_results(
    category: str | None = None,
    *,
    dataset: str | list[str] | None = None,
    methods: str | list[str] | None = None,
    metrics=None,
) -> DataFrame

Load the stored results as one long table.

The stored results are the package's own runs of its methods on the benchmark datasets, scored with mtb.evaluate. The table concatenates with the long table mtb.evaluate returns.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION category

Integration category (vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross); None = every category.

type str default None

dataset

Dataset id(s), e.g. "D11" or ["D11", "D28"]; None = every dataset of the category. mtb.catalog.datasets() lists them.

type str or list of str default None

methods

Method(s) to keep, in any case or spelling ("mofa+" -> MOFA2); None = every method.

type str or list of str default None

metrics

None / "all" = every metric; or "clustering", "batch", "classification", or a list of codes such as ["ARI", "NMI"].

type None, str or list of str default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per score: metric, value, method, dataset, category, source, scored_with. attrs["rerun_version"] holds the package version that scored the stored rows.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

No stored results for a requested category or dataset; the message names the datasets there are.

KeyError

Unknown method name in methods.

ValueError

Unknown category or metrics, or metrics names a family or code the stored results have no rows of, for example metrics="classification" on vertical.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

methods leaves no rows.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> long = mtb.load_results("vertical", dataset="D11")
>>> mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28", metrics="clustering")
See Also

mtb.evaluate : scores your own embedding into this shape. mtb.plot.bubble : draws the table.

docs.title: mtb.rank
docs.text:
rank(
    category: str,
    *,
    modalities: list[str] | None = None,
    methods: list[str] | None = None,
    metrics=None,
    long_df: DataFrame | None = None,
) -> DataFrame

The overall score and row order of mtb.plot.bubble, best first.

Within each dataset the methods are ranked on each metric; each per-dataset score is the mean rank over the metrics, min-max scaled so that the best stored method scores 1 and the worst 0, and grand_score is the mean over the datasets. Your rows are ranked against the stored rows, so these keep their scores and order. Without long_df=, the methods the package runs for the category without stored results are listed last.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION category

Integration category: vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross.

type str

modalities

Keep only methods that read all of these modalities, e.g. ["rna", "adt"], as in mtb.find_methods; None = no filter.

type list of str default None

methods

Rank only these methods, among themselves; None = every method.

type list of str default None

metrics

None = every metric present, as mtb.plot.bubble; or a family, a code, or a list of codes and families.

type None, str or list of str default None

long_df

A long table to rank instead of the stored results, such as pd.concat([mtb.load_results(category), mine]).

type DataFrame default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per method, best first: method, grand_score, needs_labels, runtime_tier, worst_sec and env.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Nothing left to rank, metrics naming a family or code the table has no rows of, long_df repeating stored method/dataset rows, your rows on another dataset than the stored rows, or modalities naming data that none of the ranked datasets measured (pass such scores as long_df=).

KeyError

Unknown method name in methods.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

One message: partial coverage, methods left out and why.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.rank("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"])
>>> free = mtb.find_methods("vertical", needs_labels=False)
>>> mtb.rank("vertical", methods=free)
>>> both = pd.concat([mtb.load_results("vertical"), mine])
>>> mtb.rank("vertical", long_df=both)

Name Summary mtb.config The paths and settings every multibench function reads.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
variable effect MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH The folder that holds the dataset folders (data_path). MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR Where method environments are installed and looked up (envs_dir). MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH Where the method scripts are, or are downloaded to on first use (repo_path). MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF A commit or tag of PYangLab/scMultiBench whose method scripts are fetched with git instead of the package's. docs.title: mtb.config
docs.text:
Settings

The paths and settings every multibench function reads.

mtb.config is one of these: set a field to change it, for example mtb.config.data_path = "/scratch/data", or set MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH, MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH and MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR in the shell. A value assigned in Python wins over the variable; None goes back to the default. print(mtb.config) shows every field; a misspelt field raises AttributeError.

ATTRIBUTES DESCRIPTION data_path

Data root that holds the dataset folders; mtb.data.fetch, mtb.scan and mtb.run use it. Default $MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH, else <base>/data.

type Path

repo_path

Folder of the method scripts (tools_scripts/), downloaded there on the first run when absent or empty. Default $MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH, else <base>/scMultiBench_scripts/<id>, where <id> changes with the scripts.

type Path

envs_dir

Where the method environments live (<envs_dir>/<env>). Default $MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR, else the first writable envs folder of the conda on PATH, else ~/.cache/multibench/envs.

type Path

leiden_flavor

Leiden backend of the clustering in mtb.evaluate: "leidenalg" (default, the paper's and the stored results') or "igraph" (faster).

type str

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.config.data_path = "/scratch/data"
>>> # before mtb.env.install(...)
>>> mtb.config.envs_dir = "/scratch/envs"
>>> print(mtb.config)
See Also

mtb.env.install : installs the method envs under envs_dir. mtb.data.fetch : downloads demo datasets into data_path.

fetch(*datasets: str, verbose: bool = True) -> 'Path | list[Path]'

docs.text:
write_example(
    dataset: str, folder: Path | str = ".", *, verbose: bool = True
) -> None

Write the example files of a tutorial dataset as .h5ad files.

The files hold a part of the dataset in the shape that your own data usually has: one .h5ad file per object, with the cell types in obs["celltype"]. The own-data section of each tutorial reads them until you put your own files in their place. They are named my_*.h5ad; the printed lines say what each holds. A file of your own with such a name is kept.

Id of a tutorial dataset, such as "D11". It has to be in the data root: mtb.data.fetch(dataset) downloads it.

type str

folder

Folder the files are written to; it is created when it does not exist. The default is the current folder.

type Path | str default '.'

verbose

Print one line per file.

type bool default True

No example is defined for dataset (the message lists the ids).

FileNotFoundError

The dataset is not in the data root; the message gives the fetch call.

>>> mtb.data.fetch("D11")

Find methods and see what each one needs. Every call works offline.

docs.title: mtb.find_methods
docs.text:
find_methods(
    category: str | None = None,
    *,
    modalities: list[str] | set[str] | None = None,
    needs_labels: bool | None = None,
) -> list[str]

Return the method ids that match every filter you pass.

A method matches when one of its variants meets category, modalities and needs_labels together.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION category

Integration category: vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross; None = any.

type str | None default None

modalities

Modalities a variant must consume, e.g. ["rna", "adt"]; "atac_peak" / "atac_gas" also select by ATAC representation. None = no filter.

type list[str] | set[str] | None default None

needs_labels

True = a matching variant needs cell-type labels; False = one runs without them; None = no filter.

type bool | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION list[str]

Method ids in the package's order.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Unknown category or modality token.

TypeError

modalities is a bare string, not a list.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.find_methods("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"])
>>> mtb.find_methods("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"], needs_labels=False)
See Also

mtb.method_info : the per-variant supports table these filters are read from. mtb.scan : which of these methods can actually run on a given dataset.

docs.title: mtb.method_info
docs.text:
method_info(method: str) -> dict

Return everything known about one method as a dict.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION method

Method id, e.g. "Matilda"; see mtb.find_methods().

type str

RETURNS DESCRIPTION dict

One flat record:

id, language, notes     the method id, 'python' or 'R', a summary
categories              the integration categories it runs in
env                     the conda env run executes it in
atac                    'peak' / 'gene_activity' / None
needs_labels            any variant reads cell-type labels
supports                one entry per variant: category, modalities,
                        output_kind, needs_labels, labels,
                        reference_batch
runtime                 measured_sec, tier, worst_sec, observed, host, note
gpu                     'required' / 'used when present' / 'not used' / 'unknown'
cpu_params              the flags that turn CUDA off on a CPU host
setup_hint              a step to take before the first run, or ''
repo_url                the upstream code the benchmark ran
reference               {doi, title, authors, journal, year}, or None
RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError

Unknown method id.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> info = mtb.method_info("Matilda")
>>> # one entry per variant: category, modalities, labels ...
>>> info["supports"]
See Also

mtb.params_for : the parameters of one variant, with upstream defaults. mtb.find_methods : filter methods by category, modalities, labels, ATAC representation.

docs.title: mtb.params_for
docs.text:
params_for(
    method: str,
    category: str | None = None,
    modalities: list[str] | set[str] | None = None,
) -> dict

Return the parameters of one method variant.

Call it before run(params=...) to see what a method accepts and what it runs with when you pass nothing.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION method

Method id, e.g. "Matilda"; see mtb.find_methods().

type str

category

Integration category of the variant: vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross; None = infer it from the other arguments.

type str | None default None

modalities

Modality tokens of the variant, e.g. ["rna", "adt"]; None = infer it from the other arguments.

type list[str] | set[str] | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION dict

method, variant ('category:mods', or several that take the same parameters), tunable (what params= can set, {name: {"type", "default"}}; default is what a run uses when you pass nothing, and None leaves it to the method's library), fixed_in_script (what the script pins, with file:line), upstream_knobs (what its library documents but the script does not expose) and upstream_url.

RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError

Unknown method, or no variant for category / modalities.

ValueError

Unknown category or modality token, or several variants with other parameters fit (the message spells out the call that selects one).

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> p = mtb.params_for("Matilda", "vertical", ["rna", "adt"])
>>> p["tunable"]["epochs"]["default"]
30
See Also

mtb.run : takes these keys as params={method: {key: value}}.

docs.title: Environments (mtb.env)
docs.text:
Install the environments the methods run in. dry_run=True shows each environment's state and download size. The environments are built for Linux and, for the methods that Windows lists, for Windows. On macOS only the dry run works.

Name Summary mtb.env.install Install the environments a set of methods needs, on Linux or Windows. Details

A run activates the installed environment folder, <envs_dir>/<env>, directly, so no conda binary is needed. When no folder exists but conda is installed, it uses conda run -n <env> instead. MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE=conda|prefix forces one mode, and prefix with no environment folder raises OSError naming envs_dir. envs_dir defaults to MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR when set. mtb.config lists the other defaults.

In prefix mode on Linux the command runs under bash -c after setting CONDA_PREFIX, putting <prefix>/bin first on PATH and sourcing <prefix>/etc/conda/activate.d/*.sh. On Windows the environment's own python.exe or Rscript.exe runs the script, with CONDA_PREFIX set and the environment's folders first on PATH.

GPU or CPU? describes the CPU and GPU builds.

docs.title: mtb.env.install
docs.text:
install(
    methods: list[str] | None = None,
    *,
    category: str | None = None,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    flavor: str = "auto",
    build: bool = False,
)

Install the environments a set of methods needs, on Linux or Windows.

Each env is unpacked from its published archive, or built from its lockfile where none is published (on Windows nothing is built: a method without a published Windows archive is refused). Installed envs are skipped. Then the method scripts are downloaded to mtb.config.repo_path if they are missing.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION methods

Method ids to cover; None = every method of category, or every method.

type list[str] | None default None

category

vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross: the methods to cover when methods is None.

type str | None default None

dry_run

True = install nothing and return each env's state and size.

type bool default False

flavor

'cpu', 'gpu' or 'auto' ('gpu' when an NVIDIA GPU is visible): the archive build of each env. An env whose methods never use a GPU takes its CPU build whatever flavor is.

type str default 'auto'

build

True = build every env from its lockfile instead of unpacking the archive.

type bool default False

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per env, the env serving the most methods first: env, methods, state ('have', 'packed archive published', 'name taken' ... on a dry run; 'PACKED', 'BUILD' after an install), flavor ('cpu', 'gpu', or 'any' for one archive for both), archive_bytes (the download) and unpacked_bytes (on disk).

RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError

Unknown method id.

OSError

A real install on a host that is neither Linux nor Windows; on Windows, a method without a Windows environment, build=True, or an archive that could not be downloaded.

RuntimeError

build=True without conda, a failed build, or a failed download of the method scripts.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.env.install(["Matilda", "totalVI"], dry_run=True)
>>> mtb.env.install(category="vertical")

docs.title: Data I/O (mtb.io)
docs.text:
Write your data as a dataset folder the methods can read, and read its canonical .h5 files back.

Name Summary mtb.io.export_dataset Write an AnnData / MuData (or loose objects) as a canonical dataset folder. mtb.io.read Read a canonical .h5 (a dataset file or an embedding.h5) as an AnnData.

docs.title: mtb.io.export_dataset
docs.text:
export_dataset(
    data,
    dataset_dir: Path | str,
    *,
    rna="X",
    adt=None,
    atac=None,
    atac_kind: str | None = None,
    labels=None,
    batch=None,
    category: str | None = None,
    adt_names: list | None = None,
    batch_index: int | None = None,
    overwrite: bool = False,
) -> Path

Write an AnnData / MuData (or loose objects) as a canonical dataset folder.

Produces the dataset folder layout (rna.h5, adt.h5, ATAC files, cty.csv), so mtb.scan and mtb.run work on your own data. Give raw counts. The files of each category are listed at https://dsichang.github.io/scMultiBench/tutorials/run/#folder-layout.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION data

Object the selector strings refer to; None when every modality is passed as an object. With a MuData, name each modality (rna='rna').

type (AnnData, MuData or None)

dataset_dir

Folder to create; its name is the dataset id for mtb.scan / mtb.run, and its parent their data_path.

type Path | str

rna

Raw-count matrix for RNA: a selector against data ('layer:counts', 'X[feature_types=Gene Expression]') or an AnnData, DataFrame or array; None = no RNA.

type (str, AnnData, DataFrame, array or None) default 'X'

adt

Raw-count matrix for protein (ADT), same forms as rna (e.g. 'obsm:protein'); None = no ADT.

type (str, AnnData, DataFrame, array or None) default None

atac

ATAC matrix, same forms as rna (e.g. 'X[feature_types=Peaks]'); None = no ATAC.

type (str, AnnData, DataFrame, array or None) default None

atac_kind

What atac holds: 'peak' or 'gene_activity'; decides the ATAC filename. None = read from the feature names: peaks (chr1:100-200) or the RNA's gene names.

type str or None default None

labels

Cell-type labels: a column, named 'obs:<col>' or '<col>' (a MuData's global .obs), '<mod>:<col>' (mdata[mod].obs), a Series indexed by barcode, or a sequence.

type (str, Series, sequence or None) default None

batch

Batch per cell, same forms as labels; splits the files per batch (rna1.h5, rna2.h5, ...) for mosaic or cross. Every cell needs a batch.

type (str, Series, sequence or None) default None

category

Integration category the folder is for (vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross); sets the ATAC and label filenames.

type str or None default None

adt_names

Protein names for the ADT matrix; they override any it carries and are needed when it has none.

type list or None default None

batch_index

Write the whole object as batch N (rna<N>.h5, cty<N>.csv); mosaic, cross or diagonal in several batches, one call per batch.

type int or None default None

overwrite

True = replace files already in dataset_dir; False = raise before writing anything.

type bool default False

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Path

dataset_dir.

RAISES DESCRIPTION TypeError

data is not an AnnData, MuData or None.

ValueError

Missing or conflicting arguments, a missing label or batch, or cells that do not pair across modalities.

KeyError

A selector names a mod, obsm, layer, obs or var column that is absent.

FileExistsError

A file this call would write exists and overwrite is False, or the folder holds files of other data.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

Values that are not whole numbers, or feature names that are missing or repeated.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, "data/MYCITE", rna="layer:counts",
...                       adt="obsm:protein", labels="obs:celltype")
>>> mtb.io.export_dataset(mdata, "data/MYMULTIOME", rna="rna", atac="atac",
...                       atac_kind="peak", labels="obs:celltype",
...                       category="vertical")
See Also

mtb.scan : confirm the folder is found and which methods can run on it.

docs.title: mtb.io.read
docs.text:
read(path: Path | str)

Read a canonical .h5 (a dataset file or an embedding.h5) as an AnnData.

matrix/data (features x cells) becomes .X (cells x features, CSR when fewer than half of the entries are non-zero), matrix/features the var_names and matrix/barcodes the obs_names. A method's embedding.h5 goes to .obsm["X_emb"] of an AnnData without features.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION path

Canonical .h5 file.

type Path | str

RETURNS DESCRIPTION AnnData RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

path does not exist.

ValueError

path is a 10x Genomics .h5 file; the message says how to read it.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> rna = mtb.io.read(mtb.config.data_path / "D11" / "rna.h5")

docs.title: Figures (mtb.plot)
docs.text:
Draw figures from a long results table: mtb.load_results returns one for the stored results, mtb.evaluate and RunResult.long for your own runs.

Name Summary mtb.plot.bubble Draw the paper's bubble table: methods as rows, metrics as columns. mtb.plot.bar Draw each method's overall score as a horizontal bar, best on top.

docs.title: mtb.plot.bubble
docs.text:
bubble(long_df, *, metrics=None, methods=None, title=None, save=None)

Draw the paper's bubble table: methods as rows, metrics as columns.

Metrics are grouped into families, each led by an Overall bar. Rows run best first, in the order of mtb.rank(category, long_df=long_df, metrics=...) with the same metrics.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION long_df

A long table (method, metric, value and optional dataset), as mtb.load_results, mtb.evaluate and RunResult.long return; stored and your own rows can be concatenated.

type DataFrame

metrics

A family ("clustering", "batch", "classification", "all"), a code, or codes in their column order; None = every metric in the frame.

type str, list of str | None default None

methods

Methods (rows) to show; None = every method in the frame.

type list of str | None default None

title

Figure title; None = "<category> <dataset>" when the table holds one of each; "" = no title.

type str | None default None

save

File to write the figure to; the suffix picks the format (.pdf, .png, .svg).

type str or path - like | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Figure RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

long_df lacks method / metric / value, repeats a (method, dataset, metric) row, holds your rows on another dataset than the stored rows, or metrics / methods names a value it does not hold.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

File to write the figure to.

docs.text:
Run the methods of a category on a dataset folder and get their embeddings. Methods run on Linux, and on Windows for the methods with a Windows environment. On macOS, mtb.scan shows the plan and its commands.

Name Summary mtb.scan Check which methods can run on a dataset, and how run would run them. mtb.run Run the runnable methods of a category on a dataset folder, and score them. mtb.load_run Reload a saved run result. mtb.RunResult The result of mtb.run: its summary table, long table and figure.

docs.title: mtb.scan
docs.text:
scan(
    dataset: str,
    category: str | None = None,
    *,
    methods: list[str] | None = None,
    modalities: list[str] | str | None = None,
    params: dict | None = None,
    assume_gpu: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = True,
    command: bool = False,
) -> DataFrame

Check which methods can run on a dataset, and how run would run them.

Nothing is executed and no file is written. Call it first on a new dataset: it prints what the folder holds and why each method that cannot run cannot.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION dataset

Dataset folder: its path, or its name under mtb.config.data_path.

type str

category

Integration category to scan; None = the benchmark's category of a dataset it scored (D11 is vertical), else all four.

type str | None default None

methods

Method ids to include, as a list; None = every method.

type list[str] | None default None

modalities

Modality tokens of one combination, e.g. ["rna", "adt"]; None = the combinations whose modalities the folder holds; "all" = every combination.

type list[str] | str | None default None

params

Parameters per method, as run takes them; they are checked and appear in command when it is asked for.

type dict | None default None

assume_gpu

True = skip this host's GPU test, to check a job for a GPU node from a login node.

type bool default False

verbose

Print what the folder holds, the cells per file and each reason.

type bool default True

command

True = add the command column: the line run would execute, with <out_dir> for the output folder.

type bool default False

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per method (per method and category when category is None), runnable methods first: method, modalities (of the variant run would run, +-joined), runnable, reason (why it cannot run), env, caveat (what to know before running it), and command with command=True.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

The dataset folder does not exist; the message lists the folders present.

ValueError

Unknown category or modality token, a method in methods without a variant there, or a benchmark dataset given another category than its own.

KeyError

Unknown method id, or a params key the method does not accept.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.scan("D11", "vertical")
>>> mtb.scan("data/MYCITE", "vertical", methods=["Matilda"],
...          params={"Matilda": {"epochs": 10}}, command=True).command[0]
See Also

mtb.run : runs the runnable methods.

docs.title: mtb.run
docs.text:
run(
    dataset: str,
    category: str,
    out_dir,
    *,
    methods=None,
    modalities=None,
    params: dict | None = None,
    batch=None,
    evaluate: bool = True,
    timeout: float | None = None,
    skip_existing: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> "RunResult"

Run the runnable methods of a category on a dataset folder, and score them.

Only the methods mtb.scan marks runnable run. A method's failure is recorded, never raised, and the results are saved under out_dir after each method. methods=["Matilda"] runs one method. mtb.scan shows the plan first, with each command.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION dataset

Dataset folder: its path, or its name under mtb.config.data_path.

type str

category

Integration category: vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross.

type str

out_dir

Output root, one <out_dir>/<method>_<dataset>/ per method. An embedding.h5 there also holds its cells' names (barcodes).

type path

methods

Method ids to run, as a list; None = every runnable method.

type list[str] | None default None

modalities

Modality tokens of one combination, e.g. ["rna", "adt"]; None = every combination the folder holds; "all" = every combination.

type list[str] | str | None default None

params

Parameters per method, {"Matilda": {"epochs": 3}}; mtb.params_for lists the keys.

type dict | None default None

batch

One batch per cell; a Series or a barcode-indexed CSV is aligned by barcode. None = each cell's label file.

type array - like | Series | path | None default None

evaluate

Score each embedding; False only runs (status ran), and a reused saved record keeps its scores.

type bool default True

timeout

Wall-clock limit per method, in seconds; None = none.

type float | None default None

skip_existing

Reuse an output already in out_dir instead of running the method again, to resume an interrupted run.

type bool default False

verbose

Print [run] ... progress lines.

type bool default True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION RunResult

Read summary first, embedding(method) for an embedding.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

The dataset folder does not exist; the message lists the folders present.

ValueError

Nothing in the selection can run, an out_dir that holds the result of another dataset or category, or a batch that does not fit the cells; checked before anything runs.

KeyError

Unknown method id, or a params key the method does not accept; checked before anything runs.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", out_dir="out/")
>>> res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", out_dir="out/", methods=["Matilda"],
...               params={"Matilda": {"epochs": 10}})

load_run(out_dir, *, methods=None) -> 'RunResult'

Reload a saved run result.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION out_dir

A run out_dir: the folder holding batch_result.json.

type path - like

methods

Methods whose records to keep; None = every record.

type list[str] | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION RunResult

The reloaded result; save() with no argument writes back to out_dir.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

out_dir holds no batch_result.json.

KeyError

A name in methods has no record; the message lists the methods that do.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

The scores were made by multibench 0.3.x; res.rescore() scores them as this version does.

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> res.summary
>>> mtb.load_run("out/", methods=["Matilda", "scMM"]).plot()

A copied run folder can be re-scored: each record's output folder is looked for next to batch_result.json when its recorded path is gone, and the dataset folder under the recorded data root, then mtb.config.data_path.

docs.title: mtb.RunResult
docs.text:
RunResult(records, dataset, category, out_dir=None)

The result of mtb.run: its summary table, long table and figure.

mtb.run and mtb.load_run build it. It keeps one record per method, which rescore and plot read.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION records

One record per method run, as run builds them.

type list[dict]

dataset

Dataset folder name the run used.

type str

category

Integration category of the run.

type str

out_dir

Where the run wrote its outputs; save() defaults to it.

type path | None default None

ATTRIBUTES DESCRIPTION records

One dict per method, as saved in batch_result.json: method, status (as in summary), out_dir (its output folder), params_used, run_sec, reused (True when skip_existing reused a saved output), metrics, labels_used (the label files in the cell order scored), error or note (the reason of summary) and the run's provenance (multibench_version, scripts_commit, env_flavor, hostname).

type list[dict]

dataset

Dataset folder name.

type str

category

Integration category.

type str

out_dir

The run's output root, or None for an in-memory result.

type path | None

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", out_dir="out/", timeout=3600)
>>> res.summary[["method", "status", "ARI", "NMI"]]
>>> res.summary[res.summary.status != "scored"]   # what did not finish, and why
>>> fig = res.plot(metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW"])
>>> res.rescore().save()                      # nothing re-run
Notes

len(res) is the number of method records.

See Also

mtb.run : produces one.

mtb.load_run : reloads one from save()'s folder.

mtb.plot.bubble : the figure plot draws from long.

docs.title: summary property
docs.text:
summary: DataFrame

One row per method: status, timing, label matching and every metric.

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per method, sorted by method:

method                  method id
status                  scored, ran, failed, skipped or timeout
ARI, NMI, ASW, ...      one column per metric
run_sec                 seconds of the method run
caveat                  scan's caveat for the method, or ""
reason                  why the method has no scores, or ""

Examples

>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> res.summary[["method", "status", "ARI"]]
See Also

mtb.load_run : reads a saved folder; its batch_result.json holds every record, with the label orders tried.

docs.title: long property
docs.text:
long: DataFrame

The scores as a long table, for plotting.

This is what plot and mtb.plot.bubble consume.

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

Columns metric, value, method, dataset, category and source. When the scores carry scored_with, so does the table. Empty, with the first six columns, when no method produced metrics.

Examples

>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> mtb.plot.bubble(res.long, metrics=["ARI", "NMI"])
>>> res.long.pivot_table(index="method", columns="metric", values="value")
Notes

Source of the rows. Each record contributes the unrounded frame run attached (or long.csv via mtb.load_run) when present. Otherwise the record contributes its metrics dict.

See Also

RunResult.plot : draws the bubble figure from this frame.

docs.title: plot
docs.text:
plot(**kw)

Bubble figure of every method that produced metrics.

Rows are methods, best first. Circle size shows the rank within a column (bigger is better). Fill compares the values in a column: the lightest is the lowest in this figure, not zero.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION **kw

Keyword arguments of mtb.plot.bubble: metrics=, methods=, title= and save=.

default {}

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Figure

Save it with fig.savefig("out.png").

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Nothing was scored (summary says why), or an unknown name in methods=.

Examples

>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> fig = res.plot()
>>> fig = res.plot(metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW"], title="D11 vertical")
>>> fig.savefig("D11_vertical.png", dpi=200)
Notes

Keywords. metrics= sets the column order and methods= a subset.

Reading the figure. Size and colour are relative to the methods in this figure, so with few methods a small gap fills the whole colour scale. Check the values in summary.

See Also

mtb.plot.bubble : the underlying function and its full keyword list.

RunResult.long : the frame handed to it.

docs.title: rescore
docs.text:
rescore(
    *, batch=None, labels=None, metrics=None, verbose: bool = True
) -> "RunResult"

Score the saved outputs again with new labels, batch or metrics.

No method is re-run. Each record's embedding is read back from its out_dir. The Leiden clusters depend on the cell order and the machine, so the same embedding can score a few hundredths differently.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION batch

Batch ids in the order of the dataset's label files, or a barcode-indexed Series or CSV. Every cell needs a batch. None = the batch run was given, else each cell's label file.

type array - like | Series | path | None default None

labels

One cell-type label per cell; a Series or a barcode-indexed CSV is aligned by barcode. None = the dataset's label files, in the order the record was scored with (ranked as run ranks them when it has none).

type array - like | Series | path | None default None

metrics

Metric family ("clustering", "batch", "classification", "all") or metric codes, which replace those scores and keep the others (with new batch or labels, only these are kept); None = every metric the batch structure allows, as in mtb.evaluate.

type str | list[str] | None default None

verbose

Print one line per method, and one before each label-order ranking.

type bool default True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION RunResult

A new result; this one is untouched. Call .save(out_dir) on it to persist it.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

The output of no method is found; the message gives the first method's error. A method that cannot be scored otherwise gets the status ran, and reason says why.

ValueError

labels or batch holds ids that are not cells of the dataset, or a cell has no batch or no label (also in the label files).

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

A Series or barcode-indexed CSV cannot be aligned and is matched by position.

Examples

>>> mtb.load_run("out/").rescore().save()
See Also

mtb.evaluate : the scoring function applied per record. RunResult.save : persist the re-scored result.

docs.title: embedding
docs.text:
embedding(method: str)

The embedding of one method, as an AnnData.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION method

A method of this result.

type str

RETURNS DESCRIPTION AnnData

obsm["X_emb"] in the method's cell order; obs_names are the cells' barcodes, each prefixed by its label file (cty2:AAAC...) when some barcode is in two files; obs holds each cell's label, and its batch when the run had more than one batch.

RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError

No record for method.

ValueError

The method did not run, or it writes a graph instead of an embedding.

FileNotFoundError

Its output folder is gone.

Examples

>>> res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", methods=["Matilda"], out_dir="out/")
>>> adata = res.embedding("Matilda")
>>> sc.pp.neighbors(adata, use_rep="X_emb")

docs.title: save
docs.text:
save(out_dir=None) -> 'Path'

Write this result to disk so it outlives the process.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION out_dir

Target folder, created if missing; None = the result's own out_dir, else the current directory.

type path | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Path

The folder written.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

The folder holds a saved result of another dataset or category.

Examples

>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> res.rescore(metrics="clustering").save("out/clustering_only")
>>> mtb.load_run("out/clustering_only").summary
Notes

Files written.

  • summary.csv - the summary frame.
  • long.csv - the long frame, only when some method produced metrics.
  • batch_result.json - dataset, category and the per-method records.
  • batch_<hash>.csv - a batch vector the records were scored with.

Saving into a folder that has a result. When the folder already holds batch_result.json for the same dataset and category, the records are merged. A method in this result replaces its earlier record, unless its status is skipped and the earlier one's is not; the other earlier records are kept, every file in the list above is rewritten from the merged set, and a line [save] Merged with 1 earlier record in <folder> (StabMap). names them. This result object is not changed. Jobs running at the same time should use one out_dir each; combine their long tables with pandas.concat to plot them together.

See Also

mtb.load_run : reads the folder back.

docs.title: Metrics (evaluate)
docs.text:
Score an embedding with the paper's metrics. The scores come as the long table that mtb.load_results returns. The API overview summarises the metrics= selector.

Name Summary mtb.evaluate Score an embedding with the benchmark's metrics.

docs.title: mtb.evaluate
docs.text:
evaluate(
    embedding,
    labels=None,
    *,
    dataset: str | None = None,
    method: str = "embedding",
    category: str | None = None,
    batch=None,
    metrics=None,
    obsm: str | None = None,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> DataFrame

Score an embedding with the benchmark's metrics.

The protocol is the paper's: Leiden clusters searched to the number of cell types for ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW and iF1, and to the number of batches for ARI_batch and NMI_batch.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION embedding

Cells x dims: an array, DataFrame, AnnData or MuData (.obsm[obsm]), or a file: .h5 (the benchmark's embedding.h5), .h5ad, .npy, .csv / .tsv.

labels

One cell type per cell: CSV path(s), a 1-D array-like, or an .obs column name ("celltype", "rna:celltype" for a MuData modality). None = the label files of dataset.

default None

dataset

The dataset folder, a name or a path; its name fills the dataset column. With labels=None its label files are read and matched to the cells by the names run writes into embedding.h5; for a file of a run folder without them, in the cell order of the method its run record names; else in the order of method when that is a package method.

type str | None default None

method

Fills the method column: a package method id or your own name.

type str default 'embedding'

category

vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross; fills the category column. With two or more batches, all but vertical add the classification metrics.

type str | None default None

batch

One batch per cell, in the forms labels takes; needed for the batch metrics unless labels lists two or more files.

default None

metrics

None = every metric the inputs allow except kBET; a family ("clustering", "batch", "classification", "all"), a code ("ARI") or a list of codes and families.

type None, str or list of str default None

obsm

.obsm key of an AnnData, MuData or .h5ad embedding; 'X' means .X. None = X_emb.

type str | None default None

verbose

Print a line when the Leiden search starts on more than 2,000 cells.

type bool default True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

The long table: metric, value, method, dataset, category, source, scored_with, one row per metric. mtb.plot.bubble draws it, next to mtb.load_results rows or alone.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Missing or misaligned labels or batches, an unknown category or metric, or batch or classification metrics without batch labels.

FileNotFoundError

An embedding, label file or dataset folder that does not exist.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.evaluate("out/Matilda_D11/embedding.h5", dataset="D11",
...              category="vertical", method="Matilda")
>>> mtb.evaluate(adata, labels="celltype", batch="sample", obsm="X_pca",
...              method="PCA")

docs.text:
Cross integration combines batches that all measure the same modalities. The task is to remove batch effects and keep the biological structure. This tutorial is for batches that each hold ADT and ATAC peaks, with no RNA. It runs StabMap and UINMF on D58mini, 3,000 cells in two batches of the benchmark dataset D58, and then on data in your own format.

Methods run on Linux. On macOS or Windows, open this notebook in Colab: sections 1 to 4 take about 6 minutes there.

docs.title: 1. Install¶
docs.text: pip may then print a note about restarting the kernel: no restart is needed, because the pins keep the numpy and pandas already installed.

docs.title: 2. Download the data and the environments¶
docs.text: mtb.data.fetch downloads D58mini (7 MB) once. mtb.env.install downloads the environments for StabMap and UINMF. The download is 0.9 GB.

docs.title: 3. Run the methods¶
docs.text:
run runs each method on D58mini and scores its output. The clustering metrics score how well the embedding's clusters and neighbourhoods match the cell types, and how separate the clusters are. The batch metrics measure how well the batches mix. The classification scores measure how well the cell types learned on one batch are predicted in the other batches. Higher is better for every metric.

Details

params={"Method": {"key": value}} sets a method's parameters, and mtb.params_for lists them.

mtb.load_run("out/D58mini") reloads these results later.

docs.title: 4. Plot¶
docs.text:
res.plot() draws the scores as a bubble table. Circle size ranks the rows within each column and colour shows the value scaled per column, so a small gap can look large. res.summary has the values.

Details

Metrics are grouped by family: blue for clustering, green for batch correction, pink for classification. Each family starts with an Overall bar: each row's mean rank over the family's metrics, scaled so that the lowest gets the shortest bar.

A column with fewer than two different values is drawn grey. A figure of one method is grey everywhere.

docs.title: 5. Your own data¶
docs.text:
Your data needs raw ADT counts in one .h5ad file and an ATAC peak matrix of the same cells in another, with a cell type and a batch for each cell.

The methods of this task read two batches.

Recipes cover a 10x .h5 file, labels in a CSV file, no labels and another number of donors.

Details: export

When the ADT file also holds a matrix in obsm under a name that does not start with X_, export_dataset asks which one is the protein matrix. X_umap and X_pca are left alone.

The batches are numbered in the sorted order of their names, read as text: donors A, B and C become batches 1, 2 and 3, and 10 comes before 2.

For one AnnData per batch, call export_dataset once per batch with batch_index=N instead of batch=.

docs.title: Cross integration: Multiple RNA + ATAC¶
docs.text:
Cross integration combines batches that all measure the same modalities. The task is to remove batch effects and keep the biological structure. This tutorial is for batches that each hold RNA and ATAC peaks. It runs StabMap and scMM on D56mini, 4,500 cells in three batches, cut from the first three batches of the benchmark dataset D56, and then on data in your own format.

Methods run on Linux. On macOS or Windows, open this notebook in Colab: sections 1 to 4 take about 8 minutes there.

docs.title: 1. Install¶
docs.text: pip may then print a note about restarting the kernel: no restart is needed, because the pins keep the numpy and pandas already installed.

docs.title: 2. Download the data and the environments¶
docs.text: mtb.data.fetch downloads D56mini (10 MB) once. mtb.env.install downloads the environments for StabMap and scMM. The download is 1.4 GB.

docs.title: 3. Run the methods¶
docs.text:
run runs each method on D56mini and scores its output. The clustering metrics score how well the embedding's clusters and neighbourhoods match the cell types, and how separate the clusters are. The batch metrics measure how well the batches mix. The classification scores measure how well the cell types learned on one batch are predicted in the other batches. Higher is better for every metric.

Details

params={"Method": {"key": value}} sets a method's parameters, and mtb.params_for lists them.

mtb.load_run("out/D56mini") reloads these results later.

docs.title: 4. Plot¶
docs.text:
res.plot() draws the scores as a bubble table. Circle size ranks the rows within each column and colour shows the value scaled per column, so a small gap can look large. res.summary has the values.

Details

Metrics are grouped by family: blue for clustering, green for batch correction, pink for classification. Each family starts with an Overall bar: each row's mean rank over the family's metrics, scaled so that the lowest gets the shortest bar.

A column with fewer than two different values is drawn grey. A figure of one method is grey everywhere.

docs.title: 5. Your own data¶
docs.text:
Your data needs raw RNA counts in one .h5ad file and an ATAC peak matrix of the same cells in another, with a cell type and a batch for each cell. Give the same peaks in every batch.

The methods of this task read three batches.

Recipes cover a 10x .h5 file, labels in a CSV file, no labels and another number of donors.

Details: export

The batches are numbered in the sorted order of their names, read as text: donors A, B and C become batches 1, 2 and 3, and 10 comes before 2.

For one AnnData per batch, call export_dataset once per batch with batch_index=N instead of batch=.

docs.text: mtb.data.fetch downloads D27mini (15 MB) once. mtb.env.install downloads the environments for iNMF and online_iNMF. The download is 0.9 GB.

docs.title: 3. Run the methods¶
docs.text:
run runs each method on D27mini and scores its output. The clustering metrics score how well the embedding's clusters and neighbourhoods match the cell types, and how separate the clusters are. The batch metrics measure how well the RNA and ATAC cells mix. The classification scores measure how well the cell types learned on one of them are predicted in the other. Higher is better for every metric.

Details

params={"Method": {"key": value}} sets a method's parameters, and mtb.params_for lists them.

mtb.load_run("out/D27mini") reloads these results later.

docs.title: 4. Plot¶
docs.text:
res.plot() draws the scores as a bubble table. Circle size ranks the rows within each column and colour shows the value scaled per column, so a small gap can look large. res.summary has the values.

Details

Metrics are grouped by family: blue for clustering, green for batch correction, pink for classification. Each family starts with an Overall bar: each row's mean rank over the family's metrics, scaled so that the lowest gets the shortest bar.

A column with fewer than two different values is drawn grey. A figure of one method is grey everywhere.

docs.title: 5. Your own data¶
docs.text:
Your data needs raw RNA counts in one .h5ad file and ATAC in another, with a cell type for each cell in both. online_iNMF needs about 5,000 cells in total.

Recipes cover labels in a CSV file and no labels.

Details: export

labels= needs the column in both files. With cell types for the RNA cells only, leave labels= out and follow the recipe for no labels.

docs.title: 6. Stored results¶
docs.text:
The package ships stored results for 11 methods on D28. load_results reads them and mtb.plot.bubble draws them, without running anything.

Details

There are no stored results for D27mini. D28 is another benchmark dataset of the same task.

docs.title: 7. Every method of this task¶
docs.text: 14 methods run this task. This notebook runs them all. Its 8 environments download 13.9 GB on a computer without a GPU and 13.2 GB on one with a GPU.

docs.title: Troubleshooting¶
docs.text:
res.summary[res.summary.status != "scored"] lists each method that failed or was skipped. Its reason column ends with the method's error output.

Details symptom fix a method fails on a small dataset mtb.scan names what the method needs from the data's size in its caveat column batch metrics use the wrong batches res.rescore(batch=...), with one batch per cell, scores again without running the methods
